dataset.description:
Experimental data describing the mechanical properties of the core wood (hybrid-aspen and poplar) material are obtained using two main testing approaches:
1) Dynamic testing – determination of elastic properties in the principal wood fiber directions, including the modulus of elasticity, shear modulus, and the characteristic dynamic parameter—the loss factor.
2) Static mechanical testing – the largest specimen group is tested using four-point bending to determine the modulus of elasticity and ultimate strength of the wood species along the principal material axes (longitudinal L, radial R, and tangential T).
Additional tests include tensile testing parallel and perpendicular to the grain to determine tensile modulus and strength, as well as shear testing in the longitudinal fiber direction.

distribution.title:
The objectives of data collection are:
1. To validate the methods used for determining dynamic and static elastic properties;
2. To obtain the characteristic mechanical properties of wood in the principal material directions (L, R, and T) for computational analysis and modeling.

dataset.title: 1.	Experimental data obtained from mechanical testing of wood properties

dataset.description: Data from SEM microstructural imaging of fast-growing wood species conducted within the project, with a particular focus on hybrid aspen. The dataset includes images illustrating structural variations within annual growth rings, as well as differences between juvenile wood and latewood.

distribution.title: The data were collected to support the homogenization of wood material properties for finite element models, as well as for micromechanical modeling in structural analyses.

dataset.title: 2.	Project data on the microstructure of fast-growing wood species

dataset.description:
Data related to numerical modeling include experimentally determined mechanical properties of fast-growing wood species used as input parameters, CAD models of wood micro- and macrostructures, and material composition configurations.
The dataset is structured around validated structural-dynamic numerical models of fast-growing wood (core material), accounting for fiber orientation, annual growth-ring structure, and earlywood and latewood characteristics. The development of the data structure follows the increasing complexity of the dynamic models, including: 
(i) a core material model, 
(ii) a simplified homogenized sandwich model, 
(iii) a multi-criteria sandwich model, and 
(iv) a structural validation model.

distribution.title: Numerical models of wood sandwich structures and their simulation results are retained to ensure access to the original model configurations and to enable their refinement and further development throughout the project implementation period.

dataset.title: 3. Experimental data generated from numerical modeling

dmp.description:
The aim of the project is to develop lightweight sandwich panel structures using fast-growing wood species—hybrid aspen and poplar—as core materials, with particular emphasis on improving vibration-damping performance. The research includes specimen manufacturing and testing to determine elastic, damping, and strength properties as a function of fiber orientation, microstructural analysis, and the development of a computational model.
The data management plan is structured around three main components:
  1. Experimental data obtained from mechanical testing of wood properties;
  2. Project data on the microstructure of fast-growing wood species;
  3. Experimental data generated from numerical modeling.
